The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: Shoppers' account pages loaded slowly
Why, in plain words: A configuration change pointed the shop's account pages at an address where their cache could not be reached, so every page had to work its figures out from scratch, which kept the pages correct but made them slow.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: 6m 18s {duration}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): none {customer_loss}
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

What was done to end it:
- Argus: rolled back the deployment of io-shop - confirmed, still in place - automatic sync left off
- Argus: proposed a fix, PR #566 - opened as a draft

Name {duration} and {customer_loss} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
Shoppers' account pages loaded slowly while deploy/values-production.yaml:cache.port was 6380
Incident: HighLatency on io-shop
Date: Nov 12, 2026, 01:37 to 01:43:18 UTC
Status: Draft. 1 of 7 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 12, 2026, 01:47:42 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 12, 2026, 01:43:02 UTC
Ended by: Argus: rolled back the deployment of io-shop - confirmed, still in place

Summary
The service broke at 01:37 UTC and was back to normal at 01:43:18 UTC, 6 minutes 18 seconds later. What its alert watches went from 26.2 ms before it began to 191 ms at its worst. The shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by no more than those hours vary on their own, if at all. A configuration change pointed the shop's account pages at an address where their cache could not be reached, so every page had to work its figures out from scratch, which kept the pages correct but made them slow. What Argus did: rolled back the deployment of io-shop (can be put back) - confirmed, still in place. Argus opened a draft fix, PR #566, for a person to review and merge. Argus left automatic sync of io-shop off, to be turned back on once its repository says what should run (AI-3). The repository still sets the cache port that refused every lookup, so syncing the repository back into production before a fix is merged could slow account pages again.

Impact
6m 18s - onset until back to normal
1.0% to 0.8% - error rate, before onset and while broken on average (no rise)
26.2 ms to 190 ms - what the alert watches, before onset and while broken on average (worst minute 191 ms; the rule's line is 100 ms)
none - customer loss (estimated)

Root cause and contributing factors
The deployment configuration's summary cache port was changed from 6379 to 6380. Nothing on the cache host accepted connections on the new port, so every cache lookup was refused. The account page handles an unreachable cache by working each shopper's spend figure out again from scratch, so pages stayed correct but became slow.
Causal chain
symptom Shoppers' account pages loaded slowly. The typical (median) time io-shop took to answer a request rose well above its usual level and stayed there, while no more requests failed than usual.
  Evidence:
    AL1 p50 latency above threshold for 5m
    T5 01:43:04 Investigator Agent: Placed the start of the incident at 01:37
why 1 Account pages could not use the rendered-summary cache. Every lookup to it was refused, so the page fell back to working each shopper's spend figure out again on each request, which is the slow path.
  Evidence:
    Gd3f7 ERROR io-shop: summary cache lookup failed - connection refused to redis://cache.io-shop.svc.cluster.local:6380 (# of 200 requests) - 8 occurrences in 8 minutes, 01:36–01:43; # was 59 to 200, typically 200, highest at 01:37
    S1 deploy/values-production.yaml at 0d8e826
why 2 The lookups went to a new cache port. Deploy P2 at 01:36:39 UTC changed the cache port in deploy/values-production.yaml from 6379 to 6380 and changed nothing else. As of 01:43:09 UTC, all 3 replicas were running that revision.
  Evidence:
    P2 01:36:39 UTC deploy 0d8e826 by kuki: from the ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App repository's deploy/ directory
    D1 Deployment of revision 0d8e826 to io-shop, compared against 544cef3 - the revision deployed before it.
    T10 01:43:09 Investigator Agent: Read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 replicas run revision 0d8e826, deployed at 01:36:39
    S1
  Ruled out:
    The earlier deploy P1 of revision 544cef3: metrics read back over the hours before the onset show the service healthy with it in place until the onset, and rolling back to it put the service back to normal.
      T4 01:43:04 Investigator Agent: Read back 361 minutes of metrics
      T5
      M1 01:43:18 Rolled back the deployment of io-shop for C1: confirmed, still in place
      T21 01:45:05 Mitigation Agent: Judged the action CONFIRMED
    A flag change by anyone but Argus: Argus read the flag provider's history - 0 flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 01:43:17.
      T16
    A change to io-shop's source code: the deploy's diff changes only deploy/values-production.yaml.
      D1
why 3 The change broke the service because nothing accepted connections on the new port, while the old port had served account pages normally.
  Evidence:
    Gd3f7
    Gad41 INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - 2 occurrences in 3 minutes, 01:35–01:37
    D1
Contributing factors
- No check was seen, in review or before the deploy, that the cache address in the deployment configuration accepts connections in production. (AI-4)
- No check was seen during the rollout that new replicas could reach the summary cache, so all replicas moved to the revision that could not reach it. (AI-5)
- No alert on refused summary cache lookups was seen. The fault was found only by the latency alert, whose rule waits with its condition holding before it fires. (AI-6)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | The deployment of 0d8e826 at 01:36:39 UTC changed the summary cache port in deploy/values-production.yaml from 6379 to 6380. Every cache lookup is now refused, so account pages render without the cached figure and p50 latency rose from about 26ms to about 190ms. The source code was not changed and the cache dependency itself is healthy. | 0.93 | confirmed

Trigger
deploy/values-production.yaml:cache.port went from 6379 to 6380 at 01:36:39 UTC, in the deploy of 0d8e826 that kuki started.

Resolution
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
M1 | 01:43:18 | Rolled back the deployment of io-shop for C1 | Argus | can be put back | confirmed, still in place - automatic sync left off
 | 01:45:59 | Proposed a fix: PR #566 | Code-Fix Agent | nothing to put back | opened as a draft

Detection
The incident on io-shop began at 01:37 UTC. HighLatency fired at 01:43 UTC, 6 minutes later.
What the alert said
AL1 | p50 latency above threshold for 5m

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Rolled back the deployment of io-shop | mitigate | Argus | - | done
AI-2 | Review and merge the proposed fix | prevent | unassigned | PR #566 | open
AI-3 | Turn automatic sync of io-shop back on once its repository says what should run - until then nothing merged reaches it, and turned on sooner it puts back what the repository says, undoing what Argus changed by hand | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Add a pre-deploy check that the summary cache host and port in deploy/values-production.yaml accept connections in the production cluster, and block the deploy if they do not. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-5 | Make io-shop's rollout stop when new replicas cannot connect to the summary cache at startup, leaving the previous revision serving. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-6 | Add an alert on io-shop's summary cache lookup failures (refused connections) and cache hit ratio. | detect | unassigned | - | open
AI-7 | Link the HighLatency alert on io-shop to an on-call rotation so that a person is paged when it fires. | process | unassigned | - | open

Lessons learned
What went well
- The alert came within the 7 minutes 30 seconds accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the onset is measured to.
- 12 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent read what the deployment of 0d8e826 changed.
- 17 seconds after the alert was raised, Argus read the flag provider's history - 0 flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 01:43:17.
- 18 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent rolled back the deployment of io-shop for C1.
- 2 minutes 5 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent judged the action CONFIRMED.
- 2 minutes 59 seconds after the alert was raised, the Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #566.
What went wrong
- Nobody was paged: the alert was linked to no on-call incident, so no person was brought in while production was slow.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

Timeline (UTC)

Response effort
none - engineer time
212,173 - tokens spent by Argus

Supporting information
The incident's walk: http://localhost:8000/incidents/d7b2ee9c-1bc5-4e8f-9783-249422b7408b
The fix it proposed: PR #566 (https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/566) opened as a draft. The record holds nothing about it after that.
Changes to production read
P1 | Nov 11, 2026, 21:36:39 UTC deploy 544cef3 by kuki: from the ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App repository's deploy/ directory
P2 | 01:36:39 UTC deploy 0d8e826 by kuki: from the ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App repository's deploy/ directory
Flags read, none came back.
Log messages read (UTC)
Gad41 | INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - 2 occurrences in 3 minutes, 01:35–01:37
Gd3f7 | ERROR io-shop: summary cache lookup failed - connection refused to redis://cache.io-shop.svc.cluster.local:6380 (# of 200 requests) - 8 occurrences in 8 minutes, 01:36–01:43; # was 59 to 200, typically 200, highest at 01:37
G46bc | ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 11 occurrences in 8 minutes, 01:36–01:43
Gbac1 | WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 7 occurrences in 8 minutes, 01:36–01:43; # was 0.50% to 2.00%, typically 1.00%, highest at 01:41
What each deployment looked into changed
D1 | Deployment of revision 0d8e826 to io-shop, compared against 544cef3 - the revision deployed before it.
modified deploy/values-production.yaml
  @@ -22,4 +22,4 @@ resources:
   # address is right.
   cache:
     host: cache.io-shop.svc.cluster.local
  -  port: 6379
  +  port: 6380
What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its fix
F1 | The fault is in deployment configuration. deploy/values-production.yaml sets cache.port: 6380. According to the investigation, the cache is healthy and listening on 6379, which was the value before deploy 0d8e826, and every lookup to 6380 was refused. This patch puts cache.port back to 6379 and changes nothing else in the file or in the repository.

No test is included. The repo's tests cover Python modules, and I can't confirm a YAML parser is installed to test this file. The way to check the fix is in production after the platform syncs it: the "connection refused to redis://cache.io-shop.svc.cluster.local:6380" lines should stop, the cache hit ratio should go back toward its normal level, and p50 latency should come back down.
What ran, read at the revision running when the alert fired
S1 | deploy/values-production.yaml at 0d8e826
Assumptions
- Exchange rate: EUR converted at 0.92191 per USD, published 2026-11-11
- No engineer minutes: no on-call incident was linked to this one, so nobody was paged to respond

Review checklist

✓ Impact assessed (met)

The document, by field:
overview: For {duration}, shoppers on io-shop found that their account pages loaded slowly. A configuration change pointed the account pages at an address where their cache could not be reached, so each page had to work out its figures from scratch. The pages still showed the right information, but they took longer to appear. Argus estimates the lost takings at {customer_loss}. Nobody was paged, and no on-call incident was linked to this one. Argus ended the slowdown by rolling back the io-shop deployment. The rollback is confirmed and still in place, and automatic sync has been left off. Argus has also proposed a lasting fix as a draft pull request. It has not been approved or applied yet.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
